text: Initialize the 16-dimensional user and video embeddings in experiment 1 with small seeded random values (for example, normal standard deviation 0.01) instead of zeros, while keeping the additive weights, pointwise binary cross-entropy objective, optimizer controls, split, and within-user evaluation unchanged. This tests whether the currently inactive low-rank interaction can learn personalized affinity rather than remaining at zero because both embedding tables start at zero.
rationale: Experiment 1 achieved primary 0.588542, GAUC 0.649869, and nDCG@5 0.527215, with identical ranking diagnostics to experiment 2, suggesting the intended interaction contribution was ineffective. The relatively stronger global AUC 0.743545 and average precision 0.551973 than GAUC indicate row-level separation does not fully translate to within-user ordering; low-rank affinity could address that if gradients can activate. Classification diagnostics show high recall 0.772897 but low precision 0.457115 and specificity 0.581240 at the F1-selected threshold, while the score distribution is non-collapsed (mean -0.845108, standard deviation 1.107645, range -5.986805 to 2.682204), so the targeted change is parameter initialization rather than score calibration or labels. It is highly feasible because it changes only initialization and remains leakage-free.
